meta.title: PharmaLens — Indian Mid-cap Pharma Intelligence
meta.author: Arunika Sherry
meta.basis: Consolidated, Indian fiscal year ending 31 March (FY22 = Mar-2022 ... FY26 = Mar-2026). Q1 FY27 = Apr-Jun 2026. All values INR crore unless stated.

sources.name: Screener.in consolidated financials (P&L, BS, CF, ratios, cost schedules)
NSE/BSE exchange filings — results, press releases, investor presentations, annual reports
Company investor relations pages (Alembic, Ajanta, Ipca, Mankind, Alkem, Glenmark)
US FDA warning letters / inspection classification database
Broker research (ICICI Securities, PL Capital, Bank of Baroda Capital) for consensus estimates
News: Business Standard, Investing.com, ScanX, Medical Dialogues, Indian Pharma Post, BioSpectrum

sector_news.title: IPM grows 13.5% in September 2026 (MAT 10.9%); volume +2.9% — growth is price/mix-led
sector_news.impact: Supports domestic-heavy names (Mankind, Alkem, Ipca, Ajanta). Volume-light growth = pricing & new launches matter more than reach.

sector_news.title: US Section 232 100% tariff on patented drugs widens; India gets zero-duty eligibility for select specialty categories; generics excluded
sector_news.impact: Generic exporters (Alembic, Ajanta, Alkem, Glenmark US) largely outside scope. Specialty/branded (Alembic Pivya, Glenmark Ryaltris) need product-level review.

sector_news.title: US President signals generics tariff path: 0% for 2 years from Aug-1, then 100%, then 200% for firms not building US plants
sector_news.impact: Medium-term overhang on US-heavy generics (Alembic 36% US, Ajanta 30%, Glenmark 27%, Alkem 20%). Triggers US-footprint / CDMO-partnering strategy questions.

sector_news.title: API, solvent & logistics inflation from Middle-East conflict flagged by Glenmark, Mankind, Alkem, Ipca on Q1 calls
sector_news.impact: Gross-margin pressure expected for 2+ quarters; backward-integrated players (Ipca, Alembic API) relatively insulated.

companies.name: Alembic Pharmaceuticals
companies.tagline: R&D-heavy US generics builder with India branded and API legs

profile.business_model: Integrated generics — US formulations, ex-US international, India branded formulations (incl. animal health) and API.
profile.description: Research-driven integrated pharma company with one of India's largest US ANDA portfolios relative to size. Invested heavily (~₹2,000 Cr+) in new oral-solid oncology, injectables, ophthalmic and derma plants at Karkhadi, Panelav and Jarod to move up the complexity curve; entered US branded specialty via Alembic Therapeutics (Pivya, Feb-2026).

footprint.market: India rank outside top-20; India branded ~30% of revenue, growing below IPM (~5% FY26). Specialty (gynaec, gastro, ophthal) growing double-digit; animal health +24% (Q1 FY27).
footprint.manufacturing: 9 facilities. US-facing formulation plants at Panelav, Karkhadi, Jarod (oral solids incl. oncology, injectables, ophthalmics, derma) — all recent USFDA audits successful. API at Panelav & Karkhadi. Indore (India formulations) WHO-certified Apr-2026.
footprint.rnd: R&D centres at Vadodara & Hyderabad. Q1 FY27 R&D ₹186 Cr (9% of sales, +29% YoY); FY27 guided ₹750–800 Cr. Focus: peptides, complex generics, specialty.
footprint.therapies_basis: Indicative weights — US approved-ANDA mix (164 OS / 33 derma / 23 ophthal / 22 inj) blended with India portfolio

regulatory.status: All US-facing formulation & API sites with recent clean USFDA outcomes.

companies.guidance: FY27: revenue mid-teens (raised); US mid-to-high teens; International ~15%; API >10%; EBITDA ~16% (core high-teens less ~150 bps Pivya dilution). ~15 US launches in 9M FY27.
data_notes: FY23 PAT depressed by impairment/one-offs; FY24 & FY26 tax rate unusually low (3%) — normalise when comparing PAT.

news.title: Alembic Therapeutics launches Clonidine HCl tablets 0.05mg in US
news.impact: Part of ~15 launches planned for 9M FY27 — feeds US momentum.

news.title: USFDA final approval for generic Ciprodex (ciprofloxacin/dexamethasone) otic suspension
news.impact: Complex sterile/otic suspension — validates move up the complexity curve.

news.title: Analyst & investor meetings (Sep-1/2, Sep-23) post guidance upgrade
news.impact: Management re-rating push; watch for working-capital commitments.

news.title: Q1 FY27: revenue +26% to ₹2,150 Cr; US +49%; PAT +12%; FY27 growth guidance raised to mid-teens
news.impact: US surge partly bosutinib (limited-competition); ex-bosutinib US +20–25%. Margin 15% held back by R&D 9% and Pivya.

news.title: Q4 FY26: PAT +29% to ₹203 Cr but EBITDA margin 12.3%; R&D 11% of sales; Pivya launched Feb-26
news.impact: Margin trough on R&D spike + branded launch costs; debt up to ₹1,430 Cr.

working: US engine accelerating: +49% YoY in Q1 FY27, 10 approvals & 7 launches in one quarter; 185 products commercialised
Deepest regulatory moat in peer set: 279 ANDAs filed / 244 approved, 152 US DMFs — complexity mix (derma, ophthal, injectables, onco) rising
Clean USFDA status across all US-facing sites — rare among peers in 2026
API (+33%) and ex-US (+17%) diversify beyond US; animal health a quiet compounder (+24%)
Backward integration into API cushions solvent/KSM inflation
not_working: Lowest capital efficiency in set: ROCE ~13% vs Ajanta 35%; ~₹2,000 Cr new-plant capex still under-absorbed
Working capital is the binding constraint: inventory 462 days, cash conversion cycle 381 days (worst in set); FY25 CFO collapsed to ₹88 Cr
India branded growth (~5% FY26) trails IPM (~10–11%) despite 5,500+ MRs
EBITDA margin stuck at ~15% (peer median ~22%) — R&D at 9–11% of sales plus Pivya dilution
Borrowings doubled FY24→FY26 (₹513 Cr → ₹1,430 Cr); finance cost +17% YoY

problems.title: Monetise the ₹2,000 Cr+ complex-generics capacity bet
problems.evidence: ROCE flat at 11–13% for 5 yrs; fixed assets + CWIP ₹3,764 Cr vs ₹7,345 Cr sales (asset turn ~1.9x vs Ajanta ~2.6x).
problems.answer: Plant-loading masterplan: map 35 pending + upcoming ANDAs to Karkhadi/Jarod lines; fill idle capacity with CDMO/third-party contracts (US tariff-driven demand for non-China capacity); line-level OEE program. Target +500 bps ROCE by FY29.
problems.investigate: Line-wise utilisation & OEE; contribution margin per SKU; launch calendar vs capacity; CDMO demand pipeline.
problems.service: Operations — Manufacturing network & OEE; Strategy — CDMO entry

problems.title: Release ₹500 Cr+ trapped in inventory
problems.evidence: Inventory days 462 and CCC 381 days (peer median ~290/150); every 30 days of inventory ≈ ₹180 Cr of cash.
problems.answer: End-to-end S&OP with US demand sensing (wholesaler 852/EDI data), SKU-tail rationalisation of the 185-product US book, API safety-stock re-optimisation, vendor-managed KSM. Target CCC <300 days in 18 months.
problems.investigate: Inventory split (RM/WIP/FG, US vs India); SKU ABC-XYZ; forecast accuracy; write-off history.
problems.service: Operations — Supply chain & working capital; Finance transformation

problems.title: Close the India branded growth gap (~5% vs IPM ~11%)
problems.evidence: India branded +7% in Q1 FY27, +5% FY26 while IPM grew ~11%; specialty divisions growing double-digit, core divisions lagging.
problems.answer: Sales-force effectiveness diagnostic (PCPM, doctor-call quality, brand-division fit); reallocate MRs to high-growth specialty (gynaec/gastro/ophthal); launch omnichannel HCP engagement; selective in-licensing for chronic.
problems.investigate: IQVIA MAT by division/brand; PCPM vs peers (~₹6–7 lakh benchmark); attrition; top-30 brand concentration.

problems.title: De-risk US concentration before the bosutinib & tariff cliffs
problems.evidence: US = 36% of revenue; reported +49% vs ex-bosutinib +20–25%; generics tariff path (100%→200%) proposed Jul-2026.
problems.answer: Product-level erosion model & launch-replacement plan; prioritise limited-competition complex filings (injectables, ophthal, peptides); tariff scenario P&L and a US-footprint option (contract manufacturing / partnership) for top-20 SKUs.
problems.investigate: Top-10 product revenue share; competitor entry timelines; tariff exposure by SKU price band.
problems.service: Strategy — Portfolio & scenario planning; Tax & Trade

problems.title: Raise R&D productivity and prove the branded-specialty model
problems.evidence: R&D ₹750–800 Cr (~9% of sales) is the highest intensity in the set yet EBITDA margin is the lowest; Pivya dilutes 100–150 bps.
problems.answer: R&D portfolio triage with risk-adjusted NPV & stage-gates; partner/out-license low-fit assets; Pivya launch-excellence & breakeven tracker (scripts, payer coverage, CAC).
problems.investigate: R&D spend per approval & per ₹ of launch revenue; Pivya weekly TRx; payer access.
problems.service: Strategy — R&D portfolio; Commercial — US specialty launch

strengths: Deepest US pipeline in the set: 279 ANDAs filed, 244 approved, 152 US DMFs
Clean recent USFDA outcomes at all US-facing plants
Backward-integrated into API — cushions solvent and KSM inflation
New complex-generics capacity: oncology, injectables, ophthalmics, derma
weaknesses: India branded growing ~5% vs Indian market ~11%
opportunities: Load the new Karkhadi, Panelav and Jarod lines, incl. CDMO for non-China supply
~15 more US launches planned in the rest of FY27
US branded specialty entry via Pivya
Animal health (+24%) and API (+33%) growing fast
threats: US generics-tariff path — 36% of revenue is US
Competition arriving on bosutinib, the current US growth driver
Normal US generic price erosion
Solvent and API cost inflation

companies.name: Ajanta Pharma
companies.tagline: Highest-return branded generics franchise across India, Asia & Africa; US scaling fast

profile.leadership: Mannalal Agrawal (Chairman); Yogesh Agrawal (MD); Rajesh Agrawal (Jt. MD)
profile.business_model: Branded generics in India, Asia (Philippines, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, etc.) and Africa; US generics; Africa institutional (anti-malarials).
profile.description: Specialty-led branded generics player — strong in cardiology, ophthalmology, dermatology and pain in India, with a 'first-to-market' launch culture (new launches outperforming IPM by 76%). Highest ROCE/RoNW in the peer group with near-zero debt and a high-payout capital return policy.
profile.employees_note: 7 manufacturing facilities, all in India; ground presence in 30+ countries

footprint.market: India branded ₹1,654 Cr FY26 (+14%), growing ~1.3x IPM; outperforming in ophthal (14% vs 9%), derma (14% vs 7%), pain (12% vs 8%) but lagging in cardiology (7% vs IPM 14%).
footprint.geography_basis: Q1 FY27 segment mix (%); Africa branded = residual
footprint.manufacturing: 7 plants in India (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar region incl. Paithan, Dahej, Pithampur, Guwahati). Paithan received USFDA EIR (VAI) in Jul-2026.
footprint.rnd: FY26 R&D ₹252 Cr (~5% of sales, up from ₹161 Cr); Q1 FY27 ₹66 Cr (4%). Advanced R&D centre in Mumbai.

regulatory.status: Paithan USFDA EIR – VAI (Jul-2026). Income-tax search (Aug-2025) – block-period returns filed Apr-2026; outcome pending.

companies.guidance: No quantified guidance; management expects continued US and India outperformance and strong cash generation through FY27.
data_notes: FY26 EBITDA includes ₹103 Cr MTM forex loss; ex-forex EBITDA ₹1,498 Cr (27%).

news.title: Sep-2026 IPM data: Ajanta +16.5% value / +7.5% units vs IPM +13.5% / +2.9%
news.impact: Volume-led outperformance — confirms India franchise health.

news.title: Q1 FY27: revenue +25% to ₹1,626 Cr; PAT +31% to ₹334 Cr; US +57%; Asia branded −16%; ₹32/share (₹400 Cr) interim dividend
news.impact: US now ~30% of sales; Asia decline is the soft spot; payout >100% of quarterly PAT.

news.title: Paithan facility receives USFDA EIR with VAI classification
news.impact: Clears path for US filings/launches from Paithan.

news.title: FY26: revenue +17% to ₹5,453 Cr; US generics +49% to ₹1,557 Cr; ROCE 33%; R&D up to ₹252 Cr
news.impact: But CFO fell to ₹529 Cr (CFO/PAT 0.5) as receivables rose — cash quality watch-point.

news.title: Block-period income-tax returns filed following Aug-2025 search; impact 'cannot be determined'
news.impact: Contingent tax overhang on retained earnings.

working: Best-in-class returns: ROCE 35%, RoNW ~27%, OPM 27–28% with near-zero debt
US generics scaling: ₹1,047 Cr → ₹1,557 Cr (+49%) in FY26, +57% in Q1 FY27 from only ~51 products — high revenue per ANDA
India branded outgrowing IPM ~1.3x, volume-led; new launches beat IPM by 76%
Gross margin expansion — material cost down from 29.5% (FY23) to 22.2% (FY26)
Shareholder-friendly capital return (buybacks + ₹400 Cr interim dividend)
not_working: Cash conversion slipped: FY26 CFO ₹529 Cr vs PAT ₹1,056 Cr; debtor days 93 → 124
Asia branded stalled (−1% FY26, −16% Q1 FY27) — the original growth engine
Employee cost creeping up: 19.0% → 24.7% of sales FY22–26; other costs to 22.2%
India cardiology growing 7% vs IPM 14% — losing share in the largest chronic therapy
Income-tax search outcome pending; borrowings up to ₹260 Cr

problems.title: Restore cash conversion (CFO/PAT 0.5x in FY26)
problems.evidence: Debtor days jumped 93→124; CFO halved to ₹529 Cr while PAT rose 15%.
problems.answer: Order-to-cash diagnostic by geography (Africa/Asia distributors, US chargebacks & rebates); credit-limit and distributor-scorecard redesign; receivables securitisation for institutional. Target CFO/PAT ≥0.9.
problems.investigate: Receivable ageing by market/customer; US gross-to-net accruals; distributor inventory levels.

problems.title: Turn around Asia branded (₹1,175 Cr, declining)
problems.evidence: −1% FY26 and −16% Q1 FY27 vs Africa branded +15%.
problems.answer: Market-by-market portfolio & route-to-market reset (Philippines, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, CIS), local brand-building, price-access strategy, tender participation; exit sub-scale markets.
problems.investigate: Country P&Ls; currency & macro effects; competitive launches; field-force productivity by country.

problems.title: Arrest cost creep in people & SG&A
problems.evidence: Employee cost +5.6 pts of sales in 4 yrs (19.0%→24.7%), highest increase in peer set; other costs 22.2%.
problems.answer: Organisation design & spans-and-layers review; MR productivity model; zero-based budgeting on promotion spend; shared-services for international back-office.
problems.investigate: Headcount by function/geography; cost per MR; promo ROI by brand.

problems.title: Build the next US growth curve
problems.evidence: US ~30% of sales on just ~51 products with 17 pending; growth may be lumpy; tariff overhang.
problems.answer: Pipeline expansion to 10–12 filings/yr with limited-competition focus; in-licensing/acquiring ANDAs; front-end channel strategy; tariff scenario model.
problems.investigate: Product-level US revenue; price erosion; filing pipeline by competition intensity.

problems.title: Win back cardiology share; enter GLP-1/semaglutide era
problems.evidence: Cardiology +7% vs IPM +14% (MAT Mar-26) while other therapies outgrow market.
problems.answer: Cardio-metabolic portfolio refresh (fixed-dose combos, semaglutide generics post Mar-2026 patent expiry), KOL & digital detailing, division split for cardio-diabeto.
problems.investigate: Brand-level IQVIA share; prescriber churn; competitor FDCs.

strengths: Best returns: ROCE 35%, EBITDA margin 27.5%
India branded outgrowing the market ~1.3x, volume-led
US generics +49% in FY26 from only ~51 products
Near-zero debt; generous capital returns
weaknesses: Cash conversion: CFO/PAT 0.5x as debtor days rose 93→124
Asia branded −1% in FY26 and −16% in Q1 FY27
Employee cost up from 19.0% to 24.7% of sales
opportunities: US pipeline: 17 pending ANDAs, 5 tentative approvals
Africa branded growing 15%
Cardio-metabolic refresh incl. GLP-1 generics
New launches outperforming the market by 76%
threats: Pending outcome of the Aug-2025 income-tax search
US generics-tariff path — 30% of revenue is US
FX volatility (₹103 Cr mark-to-market loss in FY26)
Premium valuation (P/E ~36x) leaves little room for misses

companies.name: Ipca Laboratories
companies.tagline: Integrated API-to-formulation powerhouse; Unichem integration and US re-entry underway

profile.leadership: Premchand Godha (Executive Chairman); Ajit Kumar Jain (MD & CFO)
profile.business_model: Domestic branded formulations (pain/rheumatology leadership), export formulations (branded, generics, institutional), APIs (domestic & export), subsidiaries incl. Unichem (majority stake since 2023).
profile.description: Vertically integrated manufacturer with deep API capability (HCQS, anti-malarials, cardio APIs). Strong domestic franchise in pain & rheumatology (Zerodol, HCQS). Acquired majority of Unichem Labs (2023) for US/EU generics scale; plants largely out of past USFDA embargo. Guidance raised to 14–16% growth and 23% EBITDA for FY27.
profile.employees_note: ~25 manufacturing units in India (incl. Unichem); adding ~200 MRs for a new division

footprint.market: IQVIA rank ~16, market share ~2.08%. Domestic formulations ₹3,817 Cr FY26; Q1 FY27 +13% (chronic +17.2% vs market 15.2%; acute +8.9% vs 4.5%). Anti-malarials now <1% of business.
footprint.manufacturing: ~25 units: Ratlam (API, largest), Indore SEZ, Pithampur, Silvassa, Athal, Dewas & Wardha (new API/intermediate capacity), plus Unichem (Goa, Ghaziabad, Pithampur). FY27 capex ₹700–800 Cr incl. biotech R&D.
footprint.rnd: R&D ~2–3% of sales (est.); 7 biosimilars in pipeline (revenue FY29–30); ~₹100 Cr extra FY27 for biotech pilot facilities.

regulatory.status: Own USFDA-focused plants out of embargo; 4–5 US filings/yr; 7–8 US launches FY27 (Ipca + Unichem); Ipca US +27%, Unichem US +9% (Q1 FY27).

companies.guidance: FY27: revenue +14–16% (raised from 12–13%); EBITDA ~23% (from 22%); 25–26% consolidated in 2–3 yrs (base business 30%); Unichem +10% / 13% margin; capex ₹700–800 Cr.
data_notes: Unichem consolidated from FY24 — FY24+ not like-for-like with FY22–23.

news.title: Sep-2026 IPM: Ipca +16% value / +8.4% units vs IPM +13.5%
news.impact: Domestic outperformance sustained into Q2.

news.title: Stock hits record high (+12%) on Q1; brokers raise targets (ICICI ₹2,190; PL ₹2,000)
news.impact: Re-rating on margin trajectory; valuation now ~30x FY28E.

news.title: Q1 FY27: revenue +21% to ₹2,788 Cr, EBITDA +50% (22.9% margin), PAT +72%; FY27 guidance raised to 14–16% / 23%
news.impact: Operating leverage + API recovery; personnel cost-to-sales down 141 bps.

news.title: Unichem Q1: revenue +20%, margin 11% (+680 bps YoY); API source-transfer synergies still 'minimal'
news.impact: Integration value largely ahead — key swing factor for 25–26% margin goal.

news.title: Capex ₹700–800 Cr: new API/intermediate plants at Dewas & Wardha; biotech R&D; all USD loans repaid
news.impact: Ratlam near capacity — de-bottlenecking supports API growth; balance sheet net-cash-like.

working: Margin recovery is real: material cost 35.8% (FY23) → 25.5% (FY26); EBITDA margin 15% → 21% → 24% (Q1 FY27)
Backward integration (API) = cost & supply-security moat during KSM/solvent inflation
Domestic franchise outgrowing market in both chronic (+17%) and acute (+9%)
Deleveraged: borrowings ₹1,481 Cr → ₹809 Cr; USD loans repaid; negligible interest ahead
Guidance upgraded twice; strong broker sentiment
not_working: ROCE only 17% despite margin gains — heavy asset base (₹4,627 Cr fixed assets) and 353 inventory days
Unichem drags mix: ~24% of revenue at ~11% margin vs base business ~26%
Domestic portfolio concentrated in pain/HCQS (~39% of IQVIA sales); anti-malarials −24%
Lumpy institutional & export tenders; freight/FX volatility
US regulated-market scale still small after years of import-alert legacy

problems.title: Capture Unichem synergies to close the 15-pt margin gap
problems.evidence: Unichem ~₹2,300 Cr revenue (subsidiaries line) at ~11% EBITDA vs Ipca base ~26%; API source transfers 'minimal'.
problems.answer: Synergy PMO: API source-transfer roadmap (Ipca APIs into Unichem US dossiers), joint procurement, plant network rationalisation, US/EU portfolio pruning; quantify ₹150–250 Cr EBITDA upside.
problems.investigate: Dossier-level source-change filing plan; overlap of KSMs; plant utilisation across both entities.

problems.title: Lift ROCE from 17% toward 22%+
problems.evidence: Inventory days 353; fixed-asset base grew 1.9x since FY22; capex ₹700–800 Cr planned.
problems.answer: Capital-productivity program: inventory norms by API/formulation, capex stage-gating with IRR hurdle, asset-light options (CMO for low-margin SKUs).
problems.investigate: Plant-wise capacity utilisation; inventory by product family; capex pipeline IRRs.

problems.title: Diversify domestic portfolio beyond pain/rheumatology
problems.evidence: Pain ~₹2,152 Cr of ~₹5,576 Cr IQVIA sales; HCQS single brand ~₹224 Cr; anti-malarials −24%.
problems.answer: Chronic portfolio build (cardio-diabeto, derma, onco) via new division + in-licensing; brand-lifecycle plans for Zerodol franchise; KOL programs.
problems.investigate: Brand-level growth decomposition (price/volume/new); therapy white-space map.

problems.title: Scale the regulated-market (US/EU) generics business
problems.evidence: Ipca US +27% but small base; Unichem US +9%; 7–8 launches FY27; approvals take ~1.5 yrs.
problems.answer: Integrated US go-to-market for Ipca + Unichem; filing plan prioritising limited-competition products using Ipca APIs; digital QMS to sustain compliance.
problems.investigate: US portfolio profitability; customer concentration; FDA readiness of each site.

problems.title: Industrialise tender & export demand planning
problems.evidence: Institutional +107% in Q1 (₹40 Cr spilled from Mar); freight spikes in LatAm/US/EU; FX added ~5 pts to growth.
problems.answer: Tender analytics & win-rate model, integrated S&OP across API/formulation, FX hedging policy, logistics control tower.
problems.investigate: Tender pipeline & win/loss; freight cost per kg by lane; hedge ratios.

strengths: Vertically integrated from API to formulation
Margin recovery: ~15% (FY23) to 24% (Q1 FY27)
Domestic outgrowing market in chronic (+17%) and acute (+9%)
Deleveraged — all USD loans repaid
weaknesses: Unichem: ~24% of revenue at ~11% EBITDA margin
opportunities: Unichem synergies (API source transfer, procurement): ₹150–250 Cr EBITDA over 2–3 years
FY27 guidance raised to 14–16% growth, ~23% margin
New API capacity at Dewas and Wardha
Seven biosimilars in pipeline (revenue FY29–30)
threats: Lumpy institutional and tender business
Freight and FX volatility
Regulatory history (past import alert at Ratlam)
Anti-malarials declining (−24% in Q1)

companies.name: Mankind Pharma
companies.tagline: India's #1 prescription-share franchise, scaling into specialty via BSV and innovation bets

profile.leadership: Ramesh Juneja (Chairman); Rajeev Juneja (Vice-Chairman & MD); Sheetal Arora (CEO & Whole-time Director)
profile.business_model: Domestic branded formulations (acute + chronic), consumer healthcare (Manforce, Prega News, Unwanted-72, Acnestar), BSV women's health & specialty biologics, exports.
profile.description: 4th largest by IPM value (4.7% share), #2 by volume, #1 by prescription share for 9 consecutive years (15.2%). Deep tier-2–6 reach. Acquired Bharat Serums & Vaccines (Oct-2024, ~₹13,600 Cr EV) for fertility, women's health and specialty biologics; Oct-2026 acquired 70% of Belgian CAR-T biotech ACTx (€48M).
profile.employees_note: Field force ~16,800–18,500; 32 plants in India; 7 R&D facilities with 750+ scientists

footprint.market: IPM #4 by value (4.7%), #2 by volume; therapy ranks: Gynaec #1, Acute #2, VMN #2, Chronic #3, Cardio/Diabetes/Respiratory #4–6, Anti-infectives #5, GI #6. Chronic ~40% of domestic (target 50%).
footprint.manufacturing: 32 manufacturing facilities in India (Paonta Sahib — first USFDA inspection; Udaipur & Ambernath EU-GMP). BSV biologics/recombinant capacity (Ambernath).
footprint.rnd: 7 R&D facilities, 750+ scientists; R&D ~2–3% of sales (est.). Innovation bets: Denovo Science AI drug-discovery partnership; ACTx CAR-T (70%, €48M, Oct-2026).
footprint.therapies_basis: Indicative FY26 domestic sales mix (company charts)

regulatory.status: Paonta Sahib — first USFDA inspection; Udaipur & Ambernath EU-GMP. US is a small option, not a core driver.

companies.guidance: FY27: EBITDA margin 25.5–26.5%; double-digit revenue growth; capex 6–7% of revenue; acquisition debt repaid by FY28; chronic share to 50% medium-term.
data_notes: BSV consolidated from 23-Oct-2024 — FY25 partial, FY26 full year; balance sheet step-up in FY25 is acquisition goodwill/intangibles.

news.title: Acquires 70% of Belgian CAR-T biotech Armed Cell Therapeutics (ACTx) for €48M (~₹511 Cr)
news.impact: Entry into next-gen cell therapy; long-dated, high-risk — capital allocation scrutiny while still deleveraging.

news.title: Releases pledge on 38.68% stake in BSV (Bharat Serums & Vaccines)
news.impact: Signals progress in acquisition-debt refinancing/repayment.

news.title: Q1 FY27: revenue +13% to ₹4,031 Cr; EBITDA margin 26.3% (+250 bps); PAT +29%; net debt ₹3,377 Cr (0.9x)
news.impact: Margin expansion despite ETR jump to 25.4% (Sikkim exemption expiry). CH only +4%.

news.title: Launches 'Vistar' division; acquires Rivotril brand (India) from Roche; AI drug-discovery tie-up with Denovo Science
news.impact: Portfolio depth in CNS; digital/AI R&D optionality.

news.title: FY26: revenue +17% to ₹14,278 Cr; adj. EBITDA ₹3,629 Cr (25.4%); PAT −3.4% on BSV interest & D&A; exports +34.5%
news.impact: Acquisition dilution visible in ROCE (26% → 14%).

news.title: Income-tax proceedings: adjustments of ₹1,908.66 Cr disclosed as contingent liability
news.impact: Contingent risk ~2% of market cap; management confident of position.

working: Unmatched reach: #1 prescription share 9 years running (15.2%), #2 by volume
Fastest scale-up in set: sales CAGR ~16% FY22–26; gross margin ~72–73%
BSV gives defensible specialty niches (Anti-D 100% share; Foligraf, HMG growing ~40%)
Margin expanding post-integration: 26.3% EBITDA in Q1 FY27; net debt/EBITDA down to 0.9x
Chronic moving up (~40%), cardiac +19%, anti-diabetic +13%
not_working: ROCE halved (32% → 14%) after BSV; FY26 interest ₹644 Cr and D&A ₹886 Cr compress PAT (−3.4%)
